name: Zhang Min
current_role: Chairman and President, Cofoe Medical Technology (301087.SZ / 01187.HK), Changsha
profile: Zhang Min (b. 1979, CSU EMBA) co-founded Changsha-based Cofoe with his wife Nie Juan, starting with 'Hao Hushi' home-medical stores in 2007 and launching the Cofoe brand in 2009. Cofoe makes home medical devices (monitoring, rehab, respiratory, TCM therapy, hearing) and became the first home-medical-device maker listed in both Shenzhen (A) and Hong Kong (H).
interesting_fact: Cofoe runs 600+ self-operated stores, sells through 200,000+ pharmacies and owns brands such as Beibeijia posture correctors and Jian'er Hearing (689 hearing-aid centres in 135 cities).
deep_cut_fact: The name is deliberate: Chinese 'Kefu' (可孚) draws on the classical gloss '孚，信也' ('fu' means trust), while the English 'Cofoe' comes from 'Comfortable'.
notes: Shares listing with wife Nie Juan (former vice-chair). No personal public profile; IR inbox is the best route. Background via 36kr citing prospectus: https://36kr.com/p/3797203049591561

name: Lu Shenglin
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong OPT Machine Vision Tech Co. (688686.SH), Dongguan (per third-party exec data; latest status unverified)
profile: Lu Shenglin, who holds a PhD in machinery manufacturing and automation, co-founded OPT in Dongguan in 2006 with his brother Lu Zhilin (now general manager). OPT makes machine-vision lighting, lenses, cameras and software for electronics and battery manufacturing and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He has been chairman and R&D director since May 2018.
interesting_fact: OPT has a global footprint unusual for a Chinese vision firm, with offices in Cupertino (California), Stuttgart, Tokyo, Penang, Bangkok and Vietnam.
notes: The Forbes bio says HQ is Wuxi, but the company's own site and filings put it in Dongguan, Guangdong. optmv@optmv.com is the company's general inbox (not IR-specific). Brothers Lu Shenglin and Lu Zhilin are joint actual controllers. Role source: https://www.lixinger.com/equity/company/detail/sh/688686/688686/senior-executive/shareholding-compensation

name: Christopher Urmson
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Aurora Innovation (NASDAQ: AUR)
profile: Canadian roboticist Chris Urmson led CMU's DARPA Grand/Urban Challenge teams, then spent 2009-2016 at Google's self-driving project (later Waymo), becoming project lead and CTO. In 2017 he co-founded Aurora with Sterling Anderson and Drew Bagnell. Aurora launched commercial driverless trucking in Texas in 2025 and is targeting 30,000 driverless trucks by 2030.
interesting_fact: He was technical director of the Carnegie Mellon 'Boss' team that won the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge. CMU vehicles also took 2nd and 3rd in the 2005 Grand Challenge.
deep_cut_fact: His 2005 CMU PhD thesis, 'Navigation Regimes for Off-Road Autonomy' (co-chaired by Red Whittaker), split off-road driving into efficiency-, stop- and swerve-limited regimes and cited planetary exploration and mine-mapping as low-speed cases.
notes: Born 1976 in Canada to English emigrant parents. Grew up in Trenton ON, Victoria BC, Winnipeg and Saskatoon. BSc in computer engineering, University of Manitoba, 1998. Highly relevant to tech/AI podcasts and a frequent public speaker; Aurora's press office is the best route.

name: Chi Jinhua
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Wu Xidun) of Tonze New Energy Technology Co. (002759.SZ), Shantou. Holds no listed executive title.
profile: Chi Jinhua and her husband Wu Xidun (chairman) control Shantou-based Tonze, founded in 1996 as a maker of small appliances such as ceramic stew pots. After listing in 2015 and buying Jiangsu Xintai Materials in 2016, it became mainly a maker of LiPF6, the lithium-ion battery electrolyte salt, and renamed itself Tonze New Energy.
interesting_fact: An energy-transition pivot: in 2024 Tonze earned about RMB 1.5bn from LiPF6 and fluorochemicals, versus only about RMB 208m from the kitchen appliances it was built on.
notes: Very low public profile and no executive role; husband Wu Xidun (chairman) is the public face. zwl@tonze.com is the board secretary's (Zheng Wenlong) published disclosure email in the 2024 annual report. Off the Hurun list since 2021. 'Alive' is not confirmed by any source; she is still named as actual controller in the 2024 annual report.

name: Zhou Zhiqun
current_role: Founder, Chairman, General Manager and CFO, Shenzhen Forms Syntron Information Co. (300468.SZ)
profile: Zhou Zhiqun co-founded Shenzhen Forms Syntron in November 2003 with former colleague Deng Xiusheng. The firm builds core-banking, payments and fintech software, largely for Hong Kong and Macau banks, and has worked on blockchain projects. He became sole actual controller in 2018 and took back the general manager role in 2024; the company is pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Forms Syntron filed for an H-share listing in Hong Kong but postponed the global offering in September 2026, citing market conditions.
notes: The company website lists an investor hotline (+86-755-86649962) and an investor mailbox whose source string is 'formssyntronss{name}formssi.com' (the @ sign is templated), so check the rendered page before using it. Founding and role details: https://m.rccaijing.com/news-7452912869215762038.html

name: Wang Li
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller (about 43.7% per third-party data) of Hubei Zhongyi Technology Co. (301150.SZ), Yunmeng, Hubei. No board title is confirmed.
profile: Wang Li is listed as controlling shareholder of Hubei Zhongyi Technology (founded 2007, ChiNext-listed), which makes electrolytic copper foil for lithium-ion battery anodes and electronic circuits at plants in Yunmeng and Anlu, Hubei. The chair, Wang Xiaoxia (born 1990), resigned in May 2026, and finance chief Cai Litao was elected chairman.
interesting_fact: Zhongyi is a battery-supply-chain play: its copper foil is the current-collector layer in lithium-ion cells for EVs and energy storage, and a new 10,000-tonne high-end circuit-foil line at Yunmeng reached full production in 2026.
notes: Identity is only partly confirmed: Wang Li appears as controlling shareholder on 10jqka, but no biography was found, and his relation to ex-chair Wang Xiaoxia is not stated in sources. Leadership change: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-05-30/1225339053.PDF. Best route is the board secretary contact in the company's annual report on cninfo.com.cn.

name: Eleanor Kernighan
current_role: No public role found. Private heir to the Morrison (Wm Morrison Supermarkets) family fortune.
profile: Listed by the Sunday Times Rich List (2020) jointly with William Morrison as heirs of Sir Ken Morrison (died 2017), who built Bradford's Wm Morrison Supermarkets into a national chain. A 2000 profile lists a daughter, Eleanor, and a Wikipedia mirror says she once worked as a poultry buyer at Morrisons. No public source links 'Kernighan' to the family.
interesting_fact: Sir Ken Morrison took over his father's Bradford market stall business in 1952 and ran Morrisons for more than 50 years before retiring as chairman in 2008.
notes: Very private person with no public profile or contacts, and the married surname could not be verified online. The family link rests on the Rich List pairing plus 2000 profile https://www.1in12.com/publications/Bradford/Individuals/kmorrison.html. Morrisons was taken private by CD&R in 2021. Not a podcast fit; low priority.

name: Feng Yonglin
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Chongqing Baiya Sanitary Products Co. (003006.SZ)
profile: Feng Yonglin (b. 1963) built Chongqing Baiya, maker of the Free More (Ziyoudian) sanitary-pad brand. Baiya listed on the Shenzhen main board in 2020 as China's first A-share sanitary-napkin company. It grew from a Sichuan-Chongqing base into a national top-3 brand, with RMB 3.49bn in 2025 revenue.
interesting_fact: Baiya's Chongqing plant runs 30+ smart lines with capacity of 6.7 billion pads a year, and was named to MIIT's 2025 list of 5G factories.
deep_cut_fact: Before hygiene products, Feng was head of the enterprise-management office and later deputy factory director at the Chongqing Match Factory, then ran Chongqing Huasheng tissue-paper and Sishuang hygiene-products companies.
notes: Low media profile. baiya.db@baiya.cn appears to be the board office (dongban) inbox. Investor Q&A is also possible via irm.cninfo.com.cn.

name: Wang Zhangxing
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Jiashijia Holding (Group) Co. (per a dated profile; current status unverified)
profile: Wang Zhangxing, from Shaoxing, Zhejiang, started in construction contracting and in January 2001 founded Shanghai Jiashijia Holding. The private group centres on self-operated commercial property (building-materials and home-furnishing malls, department stores, hotels) and expanded into developments in Beijing, Zhengzhou, Chengdu and Urumqi in the mid-2000s.
interesting_fact: He was ranked in the Hurun Rich List top 50 in 2005, and has appeared on Hurun China lists from 2005 through 2026.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999 he bought a former pharmaceutical warehouse on Shanghai's Yishan Road for RMB 36m to build housing. When a tenant offered RMB 10m a year in rent, he turned it into the Jiashijia building-materials mall, which grew from 15,000 to 60,000 sq m.
notes: The list's 'City' source of wealth is assumed to refer to Jiashijia's mall/'city' business, so the match is probable but not certain. The profile dates from about 2005-06. He has been president of the Shaoxing Enterprises Association in Shanghai. No published contacts found; private group.

name: Chen Zhuoxi
current_role: Non-executive Director, Agile Group Holdings (3383.HK), as of the August 2026 board list
profile: Chen Zhuoxi (Chan Cheuk Hei) is one of the brothers of Agile founder Chen Zhuolin and part of the Chen family that built Agile from Zhongshan, Guangdong into a major Chinese property developer listed in Hong Kong in 2005. He was an executive director until Agile's 2014 de-familisation reshuffle and has since been a non-executive director.
interesting_fact: The five Chen brothers (Zhuoxi is the second eldest) started with a furniture factory in Zhongshan in the 1980s and moved into property in 1992 after China's housing reform, founding Zhongshan Agile Real Estate.
notes: Listed jointly with sister-in-law Lu Yanping (Luk Sin Fong) on Hurun. Low public profile. Board role per HKEX list: https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0819/2026081900656.pdf. The IR email comes from a third-party (Moomoo) profile, so confirm it on agile.com.cn. Agile is in a debt restructuring, so be sensitive.

name: Jin Jianming
current_role: Unverified. Linked by Hurun to 'Dahua' (Shanghai Dahua Group, real estate).
profile: Hurun China (2008-2021) lists Jin Jianming with Dahua, a real-estate business, presumably Shanghai Dahua Group. That group began in 1988 in rural Dachang, Shanghai, and is now an urban-renewal developer. Public sources name Jin Huiming (b. 1953, Jiaxing, Zhejiang) as Dahua's founder-chairman. No source found ties 'Jin Jianming' to it, so this may be a name variant or relative.
interesting_fact: Shanghai Dahua Group grew from a 1988 village enterprise in Dachang, Baoshan, into a developer covering development, construction, property services, retail and hotels.
notes: Identity is unresolved: Dahua's chairman is reported as Jin Huiming (金惠明), not Jin Jianming (金建民). Check Hurun's original entry before any outreach. Off the list since 2021. Founder bio: https://www.cnpp.cn/focus/231907.html

name: Jiang Fang
current_role: Chief People Officer, Alibaba Group (since April 2023); Alibaba Partner
profile: Jiang Fang (Jane Jiang) is one of Alibaba's 1999 founding team. She held senior roles across Alibaba.com operations, marketing and credit-system development, became deputy chief people officer in 2017 and CPO in 2023, succeeding Tong Wenhong. She is a founding member of the Alibaba Partnership and was listed among its 18 partners in mid-2026.
interesting_fact: She is one of the original 'Lakeside' founding team who joined Jack Ma in 1999, and remains one of the few still in Alibaba's top leadership.
deep_cut_fact: Before running HR she led product planning for China TrustPass, Alibaba's early credit-verified membership product for Chinese SMEs, and later built Alibaba's credit system. She studied industry and foreign trade at the Hangzhou Institute of Electrical Engineering.
notes: Low external profile and rarely interviewed. Alibaba's corporate communications is the route; named media contacts on Aug 2026 releases are listed at https://www.alibabagroup.com/document-2028246284372017152. One 2025 TechNode item about partner exits is ambiguous on names, but Alibaba's official page still lists her as CPO.

name: Liu Dejian
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, NetDragon Websoft Holdings (0777.HK)
profile: Dr. Liu Dejian (Dejian Liu) studied in the US (Kansas) and ran a biotech company there before returning to Fuzhou in 1999 to found NetDragon, maker of online games such as Eudemons/Conquer Online. He later built the 91 Wireless app store (sold to Baidu) and Edmodo/Promethean ed-tech. NetDragon is now repositioning as an 'AI company' around its Moyu AI agent platform.
interesting_fact: NetDragon appointed an AI-driven virtual humanoid, 'Tang Yu', as rotating CEO of its main subsidiary Fujian NetDragon Websoft in 2022, which it billed as a world first.
deep_cut_fact: Before NetDragon's games took off, he created the game portal 17173.com, which he sold to Sohu for about US$20.5 million. Most of the proceeds reportedly went to support his mother's research work.
notes: Good podcast fit on AI and education: he gave a keynote at a UN high-level expert meeting on AI and education in June 2025. Early-life details (Kansas, US software and biotech ventures): https://www.qianzhan.com/people/profile/27c6c1.html

name: Zheng Tao
current_role: Chairman and core technical staff, Jiangsu Cnano Technology Co. (688116.SH). He stepped down as general manager in April 2026.
profile: Tao Zheng, a physicist trained in China and Canada, leads Cnano Technology in Zhenjiang, Jiangsu. Cnano is China's leading maker of carbon-nanotube conductive pastes, which raise conductivity and energy density in lithium-ion EV and storage batteries. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019. He holds about 7.6% of the company.
interesting_fact: Cnano is an energy-storage supply-chain company: its carbon-nanotube conductive agents go into lithium-ion cells for leading Chinese battery makers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cnano he was a research scientist at Bellcore/Telcordia (the former Bell Labs spin-off) and held management roles at Voltix Technology and A123 Systems, the MIT-born lithium-ion battery pioneer, including China-related work.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/battery podcast. Role change: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604291821744613_1.pdf. The career details come from a third-party (36kr) database, so confirm with the prospectus. No published email found; route via Cnano's board secretary or IR in the annual report on sse.com.cn.

name: Zheng Ming
current_role: COO of Meiwan (Meione / Mei ONE), the Shanghai company behind livestreamer Li Jiaqi
profile: Zheng Ming is COO and an early shareholder of Meiwan (Meione), set up in December 2014 by Qi Zhenbo. The company built the 'Li Jiaqi Livestream Room', China's best-known beauty live-commerce channel, plus IPs such as the 'Never family' characters and an own-brand 'Meione Youxuan' line. He appeared on the Hurun China list in 2021.
interesting_fact: Meiwan turned Li Jiaqi, a former beauty advisor at a L'Oreal counter in Nanchang, into China's 'lipstick king'. On the first day of one Tmall 618 presale his beauty livestream did RMB 4.977bn in GMV.
notes: COO role and 6.3% stake in a Meiwan-linked entity confirmed by 36kr: https://www.36kr.com/p/2306830358015232. Very low personal profile with no published contacts; approach via Meiwan corporate channels.

name: Chen Yaogen
current_role: Former Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang Yatai Pharmaceutical (Shaoxing). Current role unknown.
profile: Chen Yaogen (b. 1951), from Shaoxing County, Zhejiang, built the Yatai group, which spans pharmaceuticals (Zhejiang Yatai Pharmaceutical), real estate and textiles. He was its chairman and general manager. He appeared on Hurun China lists from 2010 to 2019.
notes: In 2021 the CSRC Zhejiang bureau issued an enforcement decision naming him over Yatai Pharmaceutical's disclosures: https://www.csrc.gov.cn/zhejiang/c103940/c3f1007aa4be7412f8dd01168bfa6de07/content.shtml. Off the rich list since 2019. Not a recommended outreach target; no published contacts.

name: Zhang Qi
current_role: Director (employee-representative) and Vice President, Shenzhen Transsion Holdings (688036.SH), if he is Zhang Qi (张祺)
profile: Transsion, the Shenzhen maker of Tecno, itel and Infinix (Africa's top-selling phones), was founded by a team from Ningbo Bird. Zhang Qi (张祺, b. 1978) worked at Ningbo Bird and Bird-Sagem, joined Transsion in August 2013, and is a director and vice president. He has been its employee-representative director since November 2025.
interesting_fact: Transsion, the 'king of Africa' in phones (Tecno, itel, Infinix), passed its HKEX hearing in September 2026 and is reported to have listed in Hong Kong in October 2026 (02636.HK) at HK$35.30 a share, giving it an A+H dual listing.
deep_cut_fact: Like founder Zhu Zhaojiang, he came up through pager and phone maker Ningbo Bird, including Bird's joint venture with France's Sagem, before joining Transsion.
notes: The input name is 张琦, but Transsion filings show director 张祺 (same pinyin). The Hurun start year of 2007 is also odd against his 2013 join date in filings, so confirm the match. investor@transsion.com is the board secretary's office contact in an April 2026 AGM notice.

name: J Mariner Kemper
current_role: Chairman and CEO, UMB Financial Corporation (NASDAQ: UMBF), since May 2004
profile: Mariner Kemper is the fourth generation of the Kemper banking family. UMB was founded in 1913 by his great-grandfather. He ran UMB Bank Colorado from 1997 and became UMB's chairman and CEO at 31 in 2004, succeeding his father. He led the 2025 acquisition of Heartland Financial USA, UMB's largest deal, and was named BankBeat's 2025 Banker of the Year.
interesting_fact: He is a trustee and executive-committee member of the Denver Art Museum, and moved to Colorado to launch UMB's commercial banking business in Denver.
deep_cut_fact: He has a personal goal of reading every primary U.S. presidential biography; Grant's memoirs became a favourite. His first job after college was checking credit-card applications at UMB, and he spent one season as a trade runner for Cargill in Chicago.
notes: Sailor and kayaker, trustee of Wetlands America (land conservation), and a political science graduate of the University of Puget Sound. Media contact Stephanie Hollander is listed in a May 2026 release; IR contact Kay Gregory is listed by phone only (816-860-7106).

name: Alexis Borisy
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Curie.Bio; Chairman of Relay Therapeutics and Tango Therapeutics; director at Revolution Medicines
profile: Serial biotech founder and investor. He started CombinatoRx in his 20s and took it public, co-founded Foundation Medicine (sold to Roche) and Blueprint Medicines (sold to Sanofi, 2025), and was a Third Rock Ventures partner for about a decade, seeding Editas and Revolution Medicines. He later founded EQRx and now runs the founder-friendly seed firm Curie.Bio.
interesting_fact: He has chaired the National Venture Capital Association, and has been personally involved in tens of billions of dollars of biotech financing and deals.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was selling peanuts at Wisconsin Badgers football games at age 14. He studied chemistry at the University of Chicago, then did graduate work in chemistry and chemical biology at Harvard as a Howard Hughes predoctoral fellow.

public_contacts.value: Dan Budwick, 1AB Media - dan@1abmedia.com (Curie.Bio press contact, 2024)

notes: A very accessible, media-friendly VC who appears on podcasts often. MIT Technology Review Innovator of the Year. Board advisor to the Boston Museum of Science. The PR contact dates from 2024, so confirm it is current.

name: Wu Kaixian
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Zonecharge / Zhongyeda Electric Co. (002441.SZ), Shantou; re-elected chairman of the 7th board in June 2026
profile: Wu Kaixian (b. 1951) founded Zhongyeda Electric in Shantou, Guangdong in 2000 after years in the industrial electrical trade. He was general manager until 2012 and has been chairman throughout. The company distributes industrial electrical products (switchgear, automation, power-distribution components) for brands such as Schneider and ABB, and is listed in Shenzhen. He controls roughly 39% of the company.
interesting_fact: He founded the company at about 49 and was still re-elected chairman for another three-year term in June 2026, at 75.
notes: Input 'Zhongyeda' = 众业达 (Zonecharge). Power-distribution equipment links to the energy and data-center theme. Low media profile. Background: https://www.lixinger.com/equity/company/detail/sz/002441/2441/senior-executive/shareholding-compensation
